Underwriters at Lloyd's London, supra, 843 F.Supp. at 606, fn. 29] (2) [3:491] Compare—employer's vicarious liability: Ins.C. § 533 does not bar coverage where an employer is sought to be held vicariously liable for intentional acts by its officers or managers that it has not authorized or ratified (see ¶ 3:114); or for statutory (FEHA) violations for which it may be strictly liable regardless of authorization or ratification. [Melugin v. Zurich Canada, supra, 50 CA4th at 667, 57 CR2d at 786; see Federal Ins. Co. v. Steadfast Ins. Co. (2012) 209 CA4th 668, 681, 147 CR3d 363, 372 (citing text)] [3:492 - 3:504] Reserved. 6. [3:505] ERISA Claims: Claims made under the Employee Retirement Income and Security Act (ERISA) relating to employee pensions or benefits plans are subject to the same coverage analysis discussed above (¶ 3:292 ff.).
